text: Proximity means nearness. Here, Phobos orbits so close to Mars that it catches rock thrown off the planet.
To stray is to wander off the right path. Here, an asteroid drifts too near Mars and gets pulled in.
A haul is the amount you gather and carry away. Here, it is the rock and dust the probe brings home.
An orbiter is a spacecraft that circles a planet without landing. It studies the planet from above.
A lander is a spacecraft built to touch down and sit on the surface of another world.
A rover is a robot vehicle with wheels that drives around on another world to explore it.
JAXA is the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency, Japan's version of NASA.
When a rocket lifts off, it leaves the ground and starts to fly. This is the start of its trip.
A probe is an uncrewed spacecraft sent to study something far away and send back information.
Phobos is the bigger of Mars's two moons. It is small and lumpy, and it circles very close to Mars.
Deimos is the smaller of Mars's two moons, about 12 kilometers across.
A planetary scientist studies planets, moons and asteroids: what they are made of and how they formed.
A long-standing puzzle is a question people have wondered about for many years without an answer.
The moons are not round like our Moon. They are bumpy and uneven, a bit like potatoes.
An asteroid is a rocky chunk left over from when the planets formed. Most circle the Sun.
Gravity is the pull between objects. A planet's gravitational field is the space around it where its pull can grab things.
Elliptical means shaped like a stretched circle, an oval. An elliptical orbit swings close to a planet and then far away.
The equator is the imaginary line around the middle of a planet, halfway between its top and bottom.
A giant collision is a huge crash between space objects. It can throw rock into space, and the rock can clump together.
Debris is scattered broken pieces left after something is smashed.
Here, gathered means pulled together into one clump, as bits of rubble slowly joined to make moons.
Hayabusa is the name of Japan's earlier spacecraft that brought back bits of an asteroid. The name means falcon.
A near-Earth asteroid has an orbit that brings it fairly close to our planet.
Organic compounds are chemicals built around carbon. They are the building blocks of living things.
Water-bearing means holding water inside. The asteroid's grains had water locked in their molecules.
Surface gravity is how strongly a world pulls on things standing on its surface. Small worlds pull only weakly.
Delicate means easy to damage. A spacecraft is delicate, so a hard landing could break it.
Touch-and-go is a quick landing: the spacecraft touches the surface for a moment and then flies away at once.
Here, kissed means touched lightly and briefly. It is a figure of speech.
To extract is to take something out. Here, the probe pulls out rock from below the surface.
Demanding means needing a lot of skill and effort. This mission is harder than earlier ones.
MEGANE is an instrument built by NASA. The name matches the Japanese word for eyeglasses.
Gamma rays are a very strong kind of light that we cannot see. Rocks can give them off when space rays hit them.
Cosmic rays are tiny fast particles from space that hit planets and moons all the time.
A fly-by is when a spacecraft zooms past something to look at it without stopping or landing.
Here, the two origin stories are the two ideas about how the moons began: captured asteroids or a giant crash.
Meteorites are pieces of rock from space that land on the ground after falling through the air.
Melt fragments are bits of rock that melted from great heat and then hardened again.
Volcanic rock forms when hot melted rock from a volcano cools and hardens.
Sedimentary rock is made when tiny bits of mud and sand pile up and press together over time, often under water.
A biosignature is a sign that life was once there, such as a chemical that living things make.
Habitable means a place where living things could survive.
Geological means about rocks and how land changes over time.
A time capsule is a box saved to show later people what the past was like. Here, the moons may hold old rock unchanged.
An astrophysicist is a scientist who studies how stars, planets and space work, using physics.
